title: Module quiz: Claude on the cloud platforms

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team sends the same traffic through a global endpoint and then a regional endpoint on Bedrock. How do the prices compare?

options.text: The two routes cost the same, since the models behind them are identical
options.says: Ruled out because the same sentence prices the two kinds differently: "Regional endpoints carry a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints."

options.text: The specific-region route costs ten percent more than the dynamic one
options.says: The page says "Regional endpoints carry a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints."

options.text: The dynamic route costs ten percent more, since it covers more locations
options.says: Ruled out because a global endpoint gives "dynamic routing across all available regions for maximum availability" with no premium.

options.text: The specific-region route costs half as much, since it uses idle capacity
options.says: Ruled out because the regional kind is the one with the premium, "10% pricing premium over global endpoints".

origin.section: Where it runs: endpoints and price

questions.stem: build_request is called for Vertex with claude-opus-5-5 and a single named region. What happens?

options.text: It raises PlatformError for the endpoint field, as newer models use other routes
options.says: The page's comment is "Specific regional endpoints support Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier; newer models use the global or multi-region endpoints", and the practice says a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only.

options.text: It builds the URL with the region host, as every model is served by those hosts
options.says: Ruled out because "Specific regional endpoints support Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier".

options.text: It falls back to the worldwide host without complaint and returns the request
options.says: Ruled out because the practice states "An unsupported model and endpoint pair is a `PlatformError`".

options.text: It raises PlatformError for the model field, as that model id is not known
options.says: Ruled out because "a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only", so the model is known and the endpoint is the fault.

origin.section: Where it runs: endpoints and price

questions.stem: A team wants the faster output option for its streamed chat, running on Opus 5.5 through AWS. What do the docs say?

options.text: The speed mode is limited to Anthropic's own endpoint
options.says: The page says fast mode "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only".

options.text: It works the same on AWS, at the same twice-standard rate
options.says: Ruled out because fast mode "is not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms".

options.text: It works on AWS for the Haiku tier alone, at the standard rate
options.says: Ruled out because the same sentence has no exception by tier: "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only".

options.text: It works on AWS once the beta header has been sent in the call
options.says: Ruled out because a header does not change that: "it is not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms".

origin.section: What Google Cloud does not offer

questions.stem: A team's Bedrock traffic needs 4 million input tokens per minute. What do the docs say?

options.text: It sits beyond every limit, so a second account is needed
options.says: Ruled out because "You can request up to 5 million input TPM" covers 4 million.

options.text: It fits inside the default, so nothing extra is asked of anyone
options.says: Ruled out because "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and 4 million exceeds it.

options.text: It exceeds the default but stays beneath the requestable ceiling
options.says: The page gives "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM without additional Anthropic approval."

options.text: It follows the direct API quota rather than the cloud one
options.says: Ruled out because "AWS enforces requests-per-minute (RPM) limits on the Bedrock side".
